outline.title: The Star and the Manger
outline.logline: Mary must find a safe, warm place to have her baby before he arrives, or she will have him in the cold street.

scenes.title: The Closed Doors
scenes.summary: Mary pauses in the narrow street under a great star, a hand on her belly, while Joseph knocks softly at the inn door and is told 'No room.' He tries three more doors along the street, and each one shuts; Mary waits in the cold, eyes on the star, and whispers that they will find a place.

scenes.title: The Last Door
scenes.summary: Under the eaves by the inn door, Mary breaks the last bread in two and shares it with Joseph, humming softly, and says again that they will find a place. Joseph hurries back to the last door, knocks, and the innkeeper says the rooms are full but the stable behind is warm and dry, and hands him a small oil lamp.

scenes.title: The Baby in the Manger
scenes.summary: Joseph clears a space and fills the wooden manger with clean straw while Mary looks from the manger to the star and nods. The lamp flickers and the wind pushes the door, and Mary's pain deepens; she takes Joseph's hand and says, 'Stay with me.' He wraps his cloak over her, sets the lamp by the manger, and lays baby Jesus in the clean straw.

scenes.title: Good News in the Field
scenes.summary: In the shepherds' field the sheep rest by the fire as the shepherd counts them under the star. Warm light floods the hillside and the angel appears; the shepherd falls to his knees, and the angel says, 'Do not be afraid — good news for all people,' and points to the star over Bethlehem. The shepherd grips his staff, takes a breath, and says, 'Come and see.'

scenes.title: Come In, Friend
scenes.summary: The shepherd steps up to the stable door, grips his staff and hangs back, but Mary smiles and offers him the bread, and Joseph says, 'Come in, friend.' The shepherd kneels slowly at the manger and looks at the child. Mary looks up through the open door at the great star, baby Jesus sleeps in the straw, and Joseph rests beside her.

premise.title: The Star and the Manger
premise.logline: Mary must find a safe, warm place to have her baby before he arrives, or she will have him in the cold street.
premise.theme: God's promise comes quietly into a humble place, and the first welcome comes from those who watch and wonder.
premise.hook: A great star burns over crowded Bethlehem, and a tired couple is turned away at every door—until one kind stable door opens.
premise.stakes: The baby will be born with no safe shelter and no welcome if they cannot find a place.

rising stakes: every door closes as Mary grows more tired
dramatic irony: we know the baby is coming before the town does
a star that leads strangers to the stable
the 'it cannot get worse' beat: the lamp flickers, the wind rises, and then the baby is born safely
premise.want: a safe, warm place to have her baby
premise.obstacle: every door in Bethlehem is closed to them
premise.clock: tonight, before Mary's baby is born

spine: Once upon a time, Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem for the Roman census, trusting God on the long road.
Every day they walked and rested, and Joseph cared for Mary as her baby grew close to being born.
Until one day they arrived at night and found every door closed, so the only shelter left was a humble stable.
Because of that, Joseph made a soft bed of straw, and Mary gave birth to baby Jesus under a bright star.
Until finally, an angel told shepherds in the field, and they hurried to the stable, where Mary and Joseph welcomed them to see the child.
Ever since then, that quiet night has been told as good news: God's promise came near in a stable, for the poor and the small.

scenes.title: The Closed Doors
scenes.purpose: Introduce Mary and Joseph, their need for shelter before the baby comes, and the obstacle of closed doors; set the stakes, the clock and the strange star.
scenes.conflict: Mary needs a warm room before her baby comes; every door in Bethlehem, starting with the inn whose stable stands at the end of the street, is closed to them.
scenes.turn: They are turned away again and again; Mary grows more tired and Joseph's worry begins to show.
scenes.moment: A voice behind the door says 'No room,' and Mary whispers, 'We will find a place.'
scenes.summary: Mary pauses in the narrow street under a great star, a hand on her belly, while Joseph knocks softly at the inn door and is told 'No room.' He tries three more doors along the street, and each one shuts; Mary waits in the cold, eyes on the star, and whispers that they will find a place.

setup.what: Mary looks up at Joseph and says, 'We need a warm place before the baby comes.'
Joseph knocks softly at the inn door; the door opens a crack, the innkeeper looks at Mary and shakes his head, and the door shuts in their faces.
Joseph takes her hand and promises, 'I will find a room before the baby comes' — so the night will not take them by surprise.
Mary stops, hand on her belly, and breathes slowly through a pain, while the great star stands high over the rooftops: the night is nearly here.
One star burns low and bright over Bethlehem, far brighter than any other in the sky; Mary lifts her face to it and Joseph looks up too.

scenes.turn: Baby Jesus is born and laid in the clean straw; Mary's fear comes out into the open and becomes joy.

beats.say: Mary stops in the street and looks up at the great star, a hand on her belly.
Mary, my dear, keep close. One of these doors will open.
Joseph holds out his cloak toward Mary.
We need a warm place before the baby comes.
Joseph knocks softly at the door.
I will find us a room before the baby comes. I promise.
The door shuts in their faces.
Do not worry for me, Joseph.
One more door, my dear. There is always one more.
Joseph walks along the narrow street from door to door.
Another door shuts.
We will find a place.
Joseph looks up at the great star.
Mary breaks the last bread in two.
Mary gives half the bread to Joseph.
Keep it. I am not hungry.
Half each, Joseph. We will find a place.
Rest here, out of the wind. One more door.
Joseph knocks at the last door.
Joseph takes the small lamp from the doorway.
The rooms are full, but the stable behind is warm and dry.
You found it. My steady Joseph.
Joseph shuts the stable door behind them.
Rest here, Mary, my dear. You carried him all this way.
Fill the straw right up. Soft for him.
Joseph takes the straw.
Joseph fills the wooden manger with clean straw.
Mary looks from the manger up at the star.
He chose this roof, Joseph.
I'm all right. It's only the cold.
I don't know what to do, Mary.
Joseph goes over to Mary.
Joseph reaches for Mary's hand.
Stay with me.
Joseph takes his cloak.
Joseph wraps his cloak over Mary.
Joseph sets the little lamp by the manger.
Joseph lays the baby in the clean straw.
My little one.
The shepherd leans on the low stone wall, counting his sheep under the great star.
The angel appears in warm light on the hillside.
The shepherd drops to his knees before the angel.
Do not be afraid. Good news for all people.
The angel points to the star over Bethlehem.
Tonight, in Bethlehem, a child is born.
Then I'll come and see the child.
They had no room for us either. Sit, friend.
Mary gets up from the ground.
Mary holds out the bread to the shepherd.
Come in, friend. No one turns anyone away here.
The shepherd goes to the manger.
I have nothing for him but a staff and a cold nose.
The shepherd kneels low at the manger.
You brought yourself. That is enough.
Mary looks up through the open door at the star.

beats.text: Mary, my dear, keep close. One of these doors will open.
We need a warm place before the baby comes.
I will find us a room before the baby comes. I promise.
Do not worry for me, Joseph.
One more door, my dear. There is always one more.
We will find a place.
Keep it. I am not hungry.
Half each, Joseph. We will find a place.
Rest here, out of the wind. One more door.
The rooms are full, but the stable behind is warm and dry.
You found it. My steady Joseph.
Rest here, Mary, my dear. You carried him all this way.
Fill the straw right up. Soft for him.
He chose this roof, Joseph.
I'm all right. It's only the cold.
I don't know what to do, Mary.
Stay with me.
My little one.
Do not be afraid. Good news for all people.
Tonight, in Bethlehem, a child is born.
Then I'll come and see the child.
They had no room for us either. Sit, friend.
Come in, friend. No one turns anyone away here.
I have nothing for him but a staff and a cold nose.
You brought yourself. That is enough.
